lessons.lesson: Host-level Falco observations can distinguish shell creation from flag-file access and support per-container attack counting without retaining raw command lines.
limitations: The source traffic was challenge verification rather than labeled player activity.
Runtime rules alone do not prove which HTTP exploit path led to a shell.
A missing runtime signal is not proof that no attack occurred.

lessons.lesson: Flag-path rules must account for exact per-target mount paths; suffix-only matching missed Target Web 05 because its flag path is /flag.txt.
limitations: The corrected Target Web 05 flag rule requires a future labeled read test to measure detection recall.

lessons.lesson: HTTP and runtime signals need request/session/process-lineage correlation before attributing a declared CVE or T1190 exploitation technique.
limitations: Current mappings cover T1005 and T1059.004 only.
No exploit-route attribution should be promoted without stronger evidence.
